children: On September 15, BlincVision will exhibit at Drive Sweden Forum in Gothenburg. The forum brings together companies and organizations working to shape the future of mobility. BlincVision will present its fast sensor technology for detection in the area close to the vehicle.

Drive Sweden is a Swedish innovation program that brings together companies, public organizations and academia to support the development of digital, connected and automated transport systems. Part of this year’s program focuses on the development of autonomous mobility in Sweden and Europe.

As vehicles become more autonomous, they need sensors that can quickly detect people, objects and movement nearby. Fast and reliable information gives the vehicle’s systems more time to react and make decisions. BlincVision’s technology is developed for situations where fast and reliable detection is critical.

“Autonomous vehicles need to understand what is happening around them and react quickly. This is exactly where our sensor technology has its strength. Drive Sweden Forum gives us a great opportunity to show what we can contribute and meet the companies and organizations working to bring autonomous solutions from development into real-world use,” says Jonas Renander, Chief Commercial Officer at BlincVision.

The company develops the groundbreaking sensor solution BlincVision. The solution enables vehicles and machines to react earlier in high-risk situations. The technology focuses on relevant changes in the field of view, allowing faster detection. The ambition is to contribute to increased safety in environments where rapid decisions are critical, from urban traffic to applications within autonomous mobility, defense and industry.
BlincVision is headquartered in Lund, Sweden, and also operates in Gothenburg.
The company is listed on Nasdaq First North Premier Growth Market.
Certified Adviser to BlincVision is Mangold Fondkommission AB, +46 8 503 015 50, ca@mangold.se.
